Subject: Request: Throughput & Latency Workbook for RFP

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As we move through our procurement round, our evaluators have asked for a detailed workbook that captures Redwood's performance characterization methodology and concrete numbers so we can compare apples-to-apples across vendors. Key asks from the RFP team:

- P95/P99 tail latency and median for token generation across short (<=128) and long (>=1024) sequences
- Sustained throughput (tokens/sec) at 50%/75%/90% cluster utilization for both single-region and cross-region configs
- Test methodology: concurrency ramp, warmup behavior, input payload distribution, and synthetic load generation approach
- Scaling behavior: horizontal scaling characteristics, autoscale thresholds, and model-variant fallback behavior under saturation
- Any caveats for quantized models, KV/prefix cache effects, and streaming vs non-streaming paths

Can you provide a workbook (spreadsheet or CSV) with the raw measurements, test vectors, and the lab setup so our SREs can reproduce the tests? We aim to finalize vendor selection by the end of November, so a response by Oct 5 would be ideal.

Also include any recommended workload profiles for our team to run (e.g., bursty chat vs steady batching).

Thanks,
Angela

Hi Angela — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a first-pass workbook that mirrors what your evaluators asked for. Highlights and what we included:

- Sheet 1: Summary (median/P95/P99 for short/long sequences across three model families we recommend for this workload: rwf-7b, rwf-13b-quant, rwf-70b-ht)
- Sheet 2: Raw measurements (per-run token times, concurrent request counts, GPU type, batch settings)
- Sheet 3: Lab test matrix (hardware, region, networking—single AZ vs cross-AZ, driver/kernel details)
- Sheet 4: Repro steps + scripts (curl/locust examples) and warmup profile recommendations
- Sheet 5: Failure modes (what we observed when we forced KV cache misses, cold-starts, and cross-region failover)

Methodology summary (short):
- Each data point is the median of 5 runs, each run is 30 minutes of steady-state or until variance <5% for tokens/sec.
- Warmup: 300s stepped ramp (0% -> 25% -> 50% -> 75% -> target concurrency) to populate KV caches and JIT heuristics.
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 concurrent requests; batch size up to 8 where applicable.
- Failure injection: network latency +10ms, 10% packet loss for 60s windows; fallbacks validated to model-variant with quantized profile.

Caveats: quantized models (4-bit/8-bit) show reduced absolute latency but increase variance under multi-tenant noisy neighbors. KV cache significantly reduces p50 for conversational workloads with repeated prefixes; we included cache-hit and cache-miss columns.

I've looped in Laura and Rishi for technical validation and legal/terms impact. We can iterate on the workbook if your team wants additional dimensions (e.g., cold-start percentiles, multi-GPU sharding).

Attached: throughput_latency_workbook_v1.xlsx, lab_test_matrix.csv, ramp-and-warmup-profiles.pdf

Next steps: if this looks good I propose a joint run — we provide a small dedicated cluster + test harness and your SREs run the workbook scripts while we observe telemetry. Proposed window: Oct 12-16.

Best,
Marcus Lin

Quick technical clarifications for reproducibility — adding here so your team can copy/paste:

- Test vectors: we used a 50/30/20 mix of short/chat prompts (<=64 tokens), medium completion (128-512 tokens), and long-generation (1024-2048 tokens). We included example prompt files in the scripts folder.
- Tokenization: measured tokens as model-token counts (BPE) not characters; we included the exact tokenizer version.
- GPU details: primary runs were on A100-80GB-like instances with CUDA 12.x, cuDNN 9.x. For quantized runs we used our trimmed kernel path; note that throughput improvements depend on memory bandwidth and whether the model fits entirely in GPU DRAM.
- Autoscale triggers: we recommend CPU load + queue-size heuristics rather than raw token-per-second thresholds to avoid aggressive scaling during transient bursts. Configs included in sheet: scale_up_when_queue>20 for worker pool size of N, cool_down 120s.
- Cross-region test detail: We ran cross-region at 25% of traffic fan-out with 200ms RTT added to simulate inter-region routing; fallback policy ensures response via a compatible model-variant within 3s.

If Vertex wants, we can provide the Locust/Vegeta command lines and a containerized harness so the runs are deterministic. Happy to include placeholder cloudformation/terraform snippets too.

- Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Angela — just following up to make sure the workbook arrived and to propose next steps. Summary:

- Workbook includes reproducible test vectors and raw per-run data for rwf-7b, rwf-13b-quant, and rwf-70b-ht.
- Key takeaways: for a steady chat-like workload (avg 64 tokens), cluster with 8 x A100-80 instances yields ~120k tokens/sec aggregate with p95 ~85ms and p99 ~220ms in single-region config; cross-region adds ~40-80ms tail depending on RTT. For long generation (>=1024 tokens) throughput drops ~6x and p99 can spike during KV-miss warmup.
- Recommended validation window: Oct 12-16 (we can provision a dedicated test pool).

Please let me know if Oct 12 works for your SREs and whether you want the containerized harness. We can also redact any proprietary kernel tuning notes if your procurement team prefers that version of the workbook.

If acceptable, Rishi will follow up on contractual/terms items related to dedicated test fleet and non-disclosure.

Thanks,
Marcus
